headlines.description: How are you affording America? That’s the thorny question NBC and Telemundo recently asked viewers in a survey. “We are struggling,” said Oakland resident Sheryl Walton. She is one of nearly 10,000 NBC and Telemundo viewers around the country who participated in the “Affording America” survey. “We always hear things about how America is so great and how things are so wonderful, but it really isn’t,” Walton said. Walton told NBC Bay Area that she’s supporting herself, her daughter, and granddaughter on one paycheck working for an airline. “I’m taking care of all of us,” she said. And she said she feels inflation is eating up her salary like never before. “I didn’t really take stock of my finances until this year when the prices skyrocketed. Gas skyrocketed. Food skyrocketed.” Jobs 14 hours ago Economy 15 hours ago Walton’s sentiment mirrors the survey. More than half of the people in the San Francisco Bay Area who took the survey, about 63%, told us they are either just getting by, struggling, or unable to consistently afford basic needs because prices have risen so high. “This is a really great snapshot of how families are struggling in America, “Lucia Walinchus, Managing Data Editor for NBC and Telemundo-owned stations. “Groceries, housing, utilities are far and away at the top of people’s lists.” We asked viewers multiple questions. Lucia then analyzed the tens of thousands of answers. Like: how much are you cutting back? “Over half of our respondents had pared back at least three expense categories,” Walinchus said. The list of respondents’ cutbacks is long. At the top: eating out (75%), travel (70%), retirement savings (55%), and groceries (53%). Walton told NBC Bay Area that she’s taken a microscope and scissors her monthly expenses. “A Saturday and a Sunday, I spent those entire days going through my expenses and my bills,” she said. “I cut close to $700 a month. I did the calculations. $685.12 or something like this.” Walton is not alone. “Consumers are looking for answers,” said Nerdwallet personal finance expert Kimberly Palmer. If you’re going to look for ways to trim your family budget, she points to three key categories: Housing, transportation, and food. Palmer said those are the three main categories that make up most of families’ spending. “About two thirds of our spending every month,” she explained. “That’s a good place to start if you can think of big ways to cut back on spending in those areas.” In Walton’s case, she says she sliced her food bill 15% by cutting out one modern convenience: delivery. “I don’t do delivery any more for my groceries. I order and I pick up. Because I figured out – duh! – it costs 10% to 15% more because they are bringing it to your door,” Walton said. With housing, Walton can’t reduce her mortgage payment. But she is micromanaging other household expenses, including her rising water bill. It was soaking her for $120 each month. So, she targeted her surprisingly thirsty lawn sprinkler. “I unplugged it,” Walton said. Her bill dropped. “Went back down $60 plus.” Walton says she’s also negotiating or re-negotiating everything, such as her cable and wireless bills, even if she’s mid-contract. She told NBC Bay Area she’s bundling or unbundling things like insurance and streaming services – wherever she can cut a deal or haggle a new discount. She says those little adjustments are making a big difference affording America. “I don’t want to live differently.” Walton said. “I still want to be able to maintain how I live, but just smarter, wiser.” In addition to NBC Bay Area’s local Affording America segments, you’ll also see them from time to time on NBC Nightly News with Tom Llamas.
